Abhimanyu.description: Son of Arjuna and Subhadra; young warrior who entered and was killed inside the Chakravyuha.

Adhiratha.description: Foster-father of Karna; husband of Radha; descended from Yayati in some accounts.

Adrika.description: An apsara cursed to become a fish; later liberated after giving birth to human children (Matsyagandha/Matsya).

Agni.description: The fire god; appears in epic contexts (see main article).

Alambusha.description: A rakshasa who fought for the Kauravas; defeated Iravan and later killed by Ghatotkacha.

Alayudha.description: Friend of Alambusha; killed by Ghatotkacha during the Night war.

Agastya.description: A venerated sage who appears in multiple Hindu texts including Mahabharata.

Amba.description: Princess of Kashi; later reborn as Shikhandi; central to Bhishma/Amba episodes.

Ambalika.description: Mother of Pandu in certain accounts; one of the royal women connected to Hastinapura lineage.

Ambika.description: Related to royal lineage and Vyasa narratives; mother of Dhritarashtra in traditional accounts.

Ambika's maid.description: Chief maid sent by Ambika and Ambalika to Vyasa; mother of Vidura by union with Vyasa in the story.

Amitaujas.description: A mighty warrior of the Panchala kingdom who fought on the Pandava side.

Arjuna.description: Third Pandava brother; preeminent archer; central figure of the Bhagavad Gita episode.

Aruni.description: Mentioned as Uddalaka Aruni in Mahabharata contexts.

Ashvapati.description: King of Madra and father of Savitri in other texts; appears in epic contexts.

Ashvins.description: Twin gods associated with medicine; invoked in various epic tales.

Ashwatthama.description: Son of Drona; fierce warrior who fought on the Kaurava side and plays a major role in post-war events.

Astika.description: Rishi figure appearing in broader Puranic/epic contexts, referenced in Mahabharata.

Ayu.description: Ancestor of Shantanu; son of Pururavas and apsara Urvashi; father of Nahusha in genealogies.

Ayoda Dhaumya.description: Sage of Avanti who accompanied the Pandavas during exile and sang Vedic songs.

Babhruvahana.description: Son of Arjuna (in some accounts) who later becomes a king in certain narratives.

Bahlika.description: A king referenced in Mahabharata genealogies and battles.

Bakasura.description: A demon encountered in sub-stories within the epic.

Balandhara.description: Princess of Kashi; wife of Bhima (in some accounts) and mother of Sarvaga.

Balarama.description: Brother of Krishna; significant divine figure who appears in Mahabharata events.

Banasena.description: Son of Karna; a mace-wielder killed during the Kurukshetra war.

Bhadra.description: One of Vasudeva's wives; mother of children in Krishna's family lineage.

Madira.description: Another wife of Vasudeva; connected to Krishna's family stories.

Bhadrakali.description: Fierce form of the Devi mentioned in epic contexts (e.g., Shalya Parva).

Bhagadatta.description: King who fought in Kurukshetra war; noted in Mahabharata lists.

Bharadvaja.description: A sage mentioned in epic lineages and narratives.

Bharata.description: Name appears in varied contexts (several Bharatas across tradition); listed among characters.

Bhima.description: Second Pandava brother; mighty mace-wielder; central heroic figure in war exploits.

Bhima of Vidarbha.description: A king named Bhima of Vidarbha mentioned in Vana Parva; father of Damayanti in certain tales.

Bhishma.description: Grand elder of Hastinapura; son of Shantanu and Ganga; commanding figure in the epic.

Bhrigu.description: An ancient sage referenced in epic genealogies and Puranic contexts.

Bhurishravas.description: Kshatriya warrior involved in Kurukshetra War episodes; mentioned in battle lists.

Budha.description: Celestial figure (son of Chandra) referenced in genealogies within epic tradition.

Brahma.description: Creator god of Trimurti; appears in mythic contexts cited by epic.

Brihadashva.description: A sage who counsels Yudhishthira and appears in narrative episodes.

Brihaspati.description: Preceptor of the gods; mentioned in various epic contexts.

Chandra.description: The moon god; appears in genealogies and mythic references.

Chandravarma Kamboja.description: Kamboja king of solar race mentioned in Adiparva; powerful ancient ruler.

Chitrasena.description: Gandharva figure referenced in epic lists and battles.

Chekitana.description: Son of Kekaya king Dhrishtaketu; valorous warrior who fought in Kurukshetra War.

Chitra.description: King of Abhisara; fought and was killed during Kurukshetra War in certain episodes.

Chitrāngada.description: Name shared by multiple figures; includes king of Kalinga and Gandharva characters.

Chitravahana.description: King of Manipura; father of Chitrangadaa and grandfather of Babruvahana.

Daksha.description: Puranic progenitor figure referenced in Mahabharata contexts.

Damayanti.description: Heroine of Nalopakhyana; referenced in Mahabharata secondary narratives.

Dantavakra.description: A king/warrior figure mentioned in epic narratives.

Danda and Dandadhara.description: Two princes of Magadha who fought for the Kauravas and were killed by Arjuna.

Darada.description: King of Bahlika; mentioned in lists and salutations.

Dasharaja.description: Fisherman chieftain of Hastinapura; father of Satyavati in tradition.

Devaki.description: Mother of Krishna; appears in Krishna family narratives referenced in the epic.

Devasena.description: Name appears in Mahabharata related lists (see main article).

Daityasena.description: Name mentioned in Mahabharata lists; related to Devasena in references.

Devayani.description: Figure related to Yayati/Shukra narratives referenced in epic material.

Devika.description: Second wife of Yudhishthira; mother of Yaudheya as per text excerpt.

Dhaumya.description: Sage who accompanied the Pandavas and served in advisory/ritual contexts.

Dhrishtadyumna.description: Son of Drupada; commander of the Pandava forces and slayer of Drona in many accounts.

Dhritrashtra.description: Blind king of Hastinapura; father of the Kauravas; central royal figure.

Dhrishtaketu.description: Ruler of Kekeya; father of warriors who participate in the war.
Dhrishtaketu.notes: Multiple rulers named Dhrishtaketu in different regions are referenced.

Divodasa.description: Ancient king referenced in epic genealogies and episodes.

Draupadi.description: Wife of the five Pandavas; central female figure around whom many events revolve.

Drona.description: Royal teacher (guru) of Pandavas and Kauravas; key Kaurava ally and commander.

Drupada.description: King of Panchala; father of Draupadi and Dhrishtadyumna.

Durmasena.description: Son of Dushasana who fought in the war and was killed by the Draupadeyas' sons.

Duryodhana.description: Eldest Kaurava brother and principal antagonist leading the Kaurava faction.

Durga.description: Goddess Durga is eulogized in parts of the epic; appears in warrior/vision contexts.

Dushala.description: Sister of the Kauravas; minor royal figure in lists.

Dushasana.description: Brother of Duryodhana; infamous for humiliating Draupadi in the royal court.

Dushyanta.description: King known from earlier legends (Shakuntala/Dushyanta episode) referenced in epic contexts.

Ekalavya.description: Skilled archer who trained himself and figures in the Drona/Arjuna narratives.

Gandhari.description: Wife of Dhritarashtra and mother of the Kauravas; known for her self-imposed blindfold.

Gandhari's maid.description: Mother of Yuyutsu in some accounts; used in the birth narrative of the Kauravas.

Ganga.description: River goddess; mother of Bhishma in the epic tradition.

Ghatotkacha.description: Son of Bhima; powerful night-fighter who fought for Pandavas and was killed in the war.

Ghritachi.description: A celestial dancer (apsara) mentioned in various Puranic/epic contexts.

Hanuman.description: Appears in Mahabharata secondary narratives; tests Bhima and imparts lessons; limited role compared to Ramayana.

Haryyashva.description: King of Ayodhya in some genealogies; husband of Madhavi; father of Vasumanas.

Hayagriva.description: Horse-headed avatar of Vishnu mentioned in mythic contexts.

Hidimb/Hidimba/Hidimbi.description: Forest demon (Hidimba) and related characters appearing in Bhima's narratives (Hidimbi wife).

Ila.description: A legendary figure referenced across Puranic and epic traditions.

Indra.description: King of gods; spiritual father of Arjuna; appears in various episodes.

Iravan.description: Son of Aravan/Arjuna in some traditions; fought and died in war narratives.

Janamejaya.description: Later descendant (of Arjuna) who appears in retellings; associated with Ramopakhyana lineage events.

Janapadi.description: An apsara who appears in origin stories of figures like Kripa and Kripi.

Jara.description: A demoness figure in certain sub-stories resulting in the birth of Jarasandha.

Jarasandha.description: Powerful king of Magadha; appears in background tales and conflicts.

Jaratkaru.description: Sage associated with family lineages and the birth of certain rishis.

Jatasura.description: Demon who attacked Pandavas in exile and was killed by Bhima.

Jayadratha.description: King who played a role in Abhimanyu's death narratives; fought against Pandavas.

Jayatsena.description: A named warrior/prince in epic lists.

Kadru.description: Mother of serpents (Nagas) in Puranic lineage; appears in Mahabharata references.

Kalaratri.description: One of the navadurgas mentioned in epic visions/dream sequences.

Kalki.description: Future incarnation of Vishnu referenced in prophetic passages (Kali Yuga context).

Kacha.description: Sage figure appearing in tales tied to the Ashvins and other legends.

Kamsa.description: Name of an antagonist king in Krishna tradition; referenced in broader epic cross-links.

Kanika.description: Sage/counselor of Hastinapur who advised Dhritarashtra in the Lac House episode.

Karenumati.description: Daughter of Chedi royal line; wife of Nakula and mother of Nirumitra in certain lists.

Karna.description: Born to Kunti and Surya but raised by Adhiratha and Radha; great warrior allied with Duryodhana.

Kauravas.description: Hundred sons of Dhritarashtra and Gandhari who oppose the Pandavas (list of names included in text).
Kauravas.notes: Text lists many individual Kaurava names.

Kauravya.description: Father of Ulupi and grandfather of Iravan in specific genealogies.

Kichaka.description: Antagonist in Virata Parva who harassed Draupadi and was killed by Bhima.

Kirmira.description: Demon encountered in Pandava exile episodes and slain by Bhima in many tellings.

Kratha.description: A Kshatriya king identified as reincarnation of Rahu in local episodes; fought for Kauravas in some accounts.

Kripa.description: Royal teacher and warrior allied with Kauravas; elder brother of Kripi.

Kripi.description: Sister of Kripa; married to Dronacharya; mother in various genealogies.

Krishna.description: Incarnation of Vishnu; charioteer and guide of Arjuna; central to the Bhagavad Gita.

Kritavarma.description: Yadava leader who fought for the Kauravas in the Kurukshetra War.

Kunti-Bhoja.description: Adoptive father of Kunti; ruler of Kunti kingdom who raised her in tradition.

Kunti.description: Mother of the Pandavas; central maternal figure involved in divine births via mantras.

Kuru.description: Eponymous ancestor of the Kuru dynasty; progenitor of Hastinapura lineages.

Lakshmana Kumara.description: Mentioned as Lakshmana in Mahabharata lists; distinct from Ramayana Lakshmana.

Lomasha.description: A rishi who appears in wilderness narratives and travel episodes.

Lopamudra.description: Figure associated with rishi traditions referenced in epic materials.

Madhavi.description: Princess figure appearing in lineage and svayamvara narratives.

Madri.description: Second wife of Pandu and mother of Nakula and Sahadeva.

Manasa.description: Serpent goddess referenced in Puranic/epic passages.

Manimat.description: King reborn as Vritra's son; fought for the Pandavas in Kurukshetra War.

Markandeya.description: Sage who narrates stories such as Nala and Damayanti in Vana Parva.

Menaka.description: Celestial apsara referenced in multiple Puranic/epic contexts.

Muchukunda.description: Kingly figure associated with ancient warrior lineages and boons.

Nala.description: Hero of Nalopakhyana referenced in Mahabharata's retellings.

Nahusha.description: Ancestor figure elevated to Indra in some legends; appears in genealogies.

Nakula.description: Fourth Pandava brother; son of Madri and the Ashvins; skilled warrior and horseman.

Nanda.description: Name appears for rulers (e.g., foster family of Krishna) and other figures in epic lists.

Nara-Narayana.description: Divine sages appearing in Vedic/Puranic tradition; referenced in epic contexts.

Narada.description: Celestial sage and messenger; appears in many episodes across the epics.

Narakasura.description: Demonic king figure referenced in Puranic tales appearing in epic cross-references.

Niramitra.description: Son of Nakula and Karenumati; minor genealogy entry.

Padmavati.description: Mentioned in Shalya Parva as follower of Kartikeya; minor character.

Parashara.description: Rishi and father of Vyasa; referenced in lineage and narrative contexts.

Parashuram.description: Avatar of Vishnu, warrior sage who appears in various epic narratives.

Parikshit.description: Descendant of the Pandavas; appears in continuation narratives.

Pandu.description: Father of the Pandavas; husband of Kunti and Madri; central ancestor in the conflict.

Pandya.description: King of Pandya who allied with Pandavas and supplied troops in the war.

Paurava.description: King involved in Kurukshetra War episodes; reborn Asura Sarabha references.

Prabha.description: Daughter of Asura Svarbhanu; married Ayu; mother of Nahusha in genealogies.

Pradyumna.description: Name tied to Yadava genealogy; appears in Puranic cross-references in epic lists.

Pratipa.description: Ancient king referenced in genealogies (e.g., father of Shantanu).

Prativindhya.description: Son of Yudhishthira and Draupadi; leader of the Draupadeyas in later lists.

Prishati.description: Chief queen of Drupada and mother of Draupadi and Dhrishtadyumna in the yajna account.

Purochana.description: Builder of Lakshagraha who set the fire; killed by Bhima when plot discovered.
Purochana.notes: Associated with the lac house conspiracy.

Pururavas.description: Ancient king whose lineage appears in epic genealogies.

Radha.description: Foster mother of Karna and wife of Adhiratha who raised Karna as her son.

Ramopakhyana characters.description: The Mahabharata contains an abridged retelling of the Ramayana; names like Rama, Sita, Lakshmana, Ravana appear here.

Revati.description: Princess figure appearing in epic genealogies and mythology.

Rohini.description: Wife of Vasudeva; mother of significant Yadava offspring in Krishna's lineage.

Rochamana.description: Kshatriya king who fought for Pandavas and was killed by Karna in Kurukshetra War.

Rukmi.description: Brother of Rukmini; has roles in Krishna/Rukmini narratives and allied episodes.

Rukmini.description: Consort of Krishna; appears in Yadava line references.

Ruru.description: Rishi mentioned in epic narratives; father of Sunaka in lists.

Sahadeva.description: Youngest Pandava brother; son of Madri and the Ashvins; known for wisdom and astrology in some tellings.

Sakradeva.description: Crown prince of Kalinga who fought and was killed by Bhima.

Samba.description: Son of Krishna; appears in post-war Yadava narratives and later histories.

Samudrasena.description: A king defeated by Bhima during conquests and later killed in the Kurukshetra War.

Shamika.description: Sage involved in Parikshit's tale; his son Sringin and curse episodes appear in narrative.

Shiva.description: Supreme deity (part of Trimurti) referenced throughout epic contexts.

Shri.description: Divine feminine principle; used in contexts like Lakshmi and Draupadi associations.

Samvarana.description: Ancestor figure in Kuru lineage mentioned in genealogies.

Sanjaya.description: Charioteer/attendant who narrates the battle to Dhritarashtra (visionary narrator).

Sarama.description: Divine hound or figure appearing in mythic contexts; appears in epic references.

Sarasvati.description: Goddess of knowledge and speech; referenced in Mahabharata passages.

Satyabhama.description: Consort of Krishna appearing in Yadava narratives and later references.

Satyajit.description: One of Drupada's sons; listed among the Panchala nobles.

Satyaki.description: Valiant Yadava warrior allied with the Pandavas in the Kurukshetra War.

Satyavati.description: Mother of Vyasa; grandmother of Pandu and Dhritarashtra; key matriarch in Kuru line.

Savitri (goddess).description: Consort of Brahma referenced in classical tales such as Savitri and Satyavan.

Savitri and Satyavan.description: Famous tale referenced within epic tradition; Savitri pleads for her husband's life from Yama.

Senavindu.description: King mentioned as a warrior who was defeated by Arjuna during digvijaya.

Shachi.description: Consort of Indra (also called Indrani); appears in divine catalogues.

Shakuni.description: Maternal uncle of the Kauravas; master manipulator and prime instigator of many plots.

Shakuntala.description: Heroine of Shakuntala/Dushyanta story referenced in epic tradition.

Shalva.description: King of Shalva who sought Amba and appears in conflicts following Bhishma's svayamvara.

Shalya.description: King of Madra who fights on Kaurava side as commander; has three sons named in lists.

Sons of Shalya.description: Madranjaya, Rukmanagada, and Rukmanaratha — sons of Shalya who fought and died in the war.

Shankha.description: Third son of King Virata; killed by Bhishma in the Kurukshetra war.

Shantanu.description: King of Hastinapura; father of Bhishma; central ancestor in Kuru dynasty stories.

Sharmishtha.description: Princess connected to Yayati/Shukra narratives; appears in Puranic/epic cross references.

Shatanika.description: Son of Nakula and Draupadi (a Draupadeya) mentioned in descendant lists.

Shaunaka.description: Headed sages during sacrifice where Ugrashravas recited the Mahabharata.

Shikhandi.description: Reborn Amba (in many tellings); instrumental in Bhishma's fall during the war.

Shishupala.description: King who opposed Krishna; killed by Krishna during Rajasuya context in some accounts.

Sons of Shishupala.description: Four sons including Dhrishtaketu, Mahipala, Suketu, Sarabha; appear in battle lists.

Shrutakarma.description: Son of Arjuna and Draupadi; youngest among Draupadeyas in lists.

Shrutasena.description: Son of Sahadeva and Draupadi; listed among Draupadeyas.

Shrutayudha.description: A warrior mentioned in epic lists (see main article).

Shukra.description: Preceptor of the asuras; father of Devayani; features in earlier myths referenced in epic.

Shveta.description: Second son of Virata killed early in the Kurukshetra war by Bhishma.

Shvetaki.description: King who performed yajnas; related to the Khandava Dahana episode.

Shreniman.description: King of Kumaradesa who fought for the Pandavas and was killed by Drona.

Subala.description: King of Gandhara; father of Shakuni and Gandhari.

Subhadra.description: Sister of Krishna; wife of Arjuna and mother of Abhimanyu.

Sudakshina.description: King who appears among supporting allies in the epic's battle lists.

Sudeshna.description: Queen of Matsya who appears in Virata Parva narratives.

Sunaka.description: Son of Ruru and Pramadvara; member of Yudhishthira's assembly.

Surya.description: Sun god; invoked by Kunti to beget Karna; appears in multiple epic episodes.

Susharma.description: King of Trigarta who supported the Kauravas and was killed by Arjuna.

Sutasoma.description: Son of Bhima and Draupadi; listed among Draupadeyas.

Svaha.description: Goddess associated with sacrificial offerings; noted in lists.

Takshaka.description: King of snakes; involved in later tales such as Parikshit's death.

Tapati.description: River goddess mentioned in epic mythic references.

Tilottama.description: A celestial apsara famed for beauty; figures in mythic lists and episodes.

Tara.description: Name shared by multiple figures (e.g., Tara the vanara queen in Ramayana tradition and other Taras in Puranic stories); present in Mahabharata references.

Ugrasena.description: King of the Yadavas in later Krishna narratives; appears in Yadava genealogies.

Ugrashravas Sauti.description: The bard/scholar who recites the Mahabharata to sages; central framing narrator.

Uluka.description: Son of Shakuni; acted as messenger/commander for Kaurava side in some episodes.

Ulupi.description: Naga princess who married Arjuna and bore Iravan in some versions.

Uma.description: Consort of Shiva (Parvati); appears in mythic cross-references within epic.

Uparichara Vasu.description: King whose legend is recounted in Vedic/Puranic traditions and referenced in epic genealogies.

Urvashi.description: Celestial nymph whose interactions with kings and sages appear in different tales referenced by the epic.

Ushinara.description: King of the Bhojas referenced among allies and genealogies.

Uttamaujas.description: Warrior who serves Pandava side; appears in Kurukshetra battle lists.

Uttanka.description: Rishi figure appearing in narrative and parable sequences.

Uttara.description: Name used for multiple figures (e.g., son of Virata in Virata Parva; also name of princess Uttarā who marries Abhimanyu).

Uttarā.description: Princess of Virata; wife of Abhimanyu and mother of Parikshit in many accounts.

Vajra.description: Son of Aniruddha; later crowned in Indraprastha lineage in post-war retellings.

Vapusthama.description: Princess of Kashi; descendant of Bhima; married into Janamejaya's line in some tales.

Varaha.description: Boar-incarnation of Vishnu referenced in Vana Parva narratives.

Varuna.description: God of waters; appears in mythic and ritual references in the epic.

Vasishtha.description: Royal sage and spiritual advisor referenced across epic tradition.

Vasudeva.description: Father of Krishna; appears in Yadava genealogies and Krishna narratives.

Vayu.description: God of wind; spiritual father of Bhima and Hanuman in lore; invoked in epic genealogies.

Virabhadra.description: Fierce form of Shiva who destroys Daksha's yajna; referenced in Shanti Parva.

Vichitravirya.description: King of Hastinapura; brother of Chitrangada and father figure in Kuru lineage stories.

Vidura.description: Half-brother of Dhritarashtra and prime minister of Hastinapura; moral advisor figure.

Vidura's wife.description: Wife of Vidura (Sulabha in later versions) noted for piety and devotion; appears in Krishna visit anecdotes.

Vijayā.description: Daughter of Dyutimata of Madra; wife of Sahadeva in some accounts.

Vikarna.description: One of the Kaurava princes; noted for moral questioning among Kauravas in some versions.

Vinata.description: Mother of Garuda in Puranic tradition; appears in epic reference lists.

Vinda and Anuvinda.description: Twin kings of Avanti who fought on the Kaurava side in Kurukshetra war.

Virata.description: King of Matsya who hosted the Pandavas during their incognito year; father of Uttarā.

Virini.description: Goddess figure referenced in some Puranic/epic lists.

Vishnu.description: Supreme preserver deity; Krishna is his incarnation in the epic.

Vishoka.description: Charioteer of Bhima during the Kurukshetra War as per lists.

Vishvamitra.description: Sage who was once a king; appears in multiple epic episodes and lineages.

Vrihanta.description: Named king/warrior in epic lists and battle accounts.

Vridhakshtra.description: Former king of Singhu; father of Jayadratha and Vijayadratha; later became a rishi in some tales.

Vrishaketu.description: Son of Karna who survives into later lineages after the war in many retellings.

Vrishasena.description: Son of Karna who fought in the Kurukshetra War and was killed.

Vyasa.description: Veda Vyasa, traditionally credited with composing the Mahabharata; central sage in the text.

Yama.description: God of death and Dharma; spiritual father of Yudhishthira and appears in the Yaksha tales.

Yaudheya.description: Son of Yudhishthira and Devika; appears in later genealogical lists and Purana cross-references.

Yayati.description: Ancestor king referenced across Puranic genealogies and epic tradition.

Yudhamanyu.description: Warrior mentioned in epic lists; one of the heroes in expansion narratives.

Yudhishthira.description: Eldest Pandava brother; known for adherence to dharma and later king of Indraprastha/Hastinapura.

Yuyutsu.description: Son of Dhritarashtra by a maid; sided with Pandavas and survived the war in many tellings.
